sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the eternal aspect of the manna, showing that in every place, time, and situation, a Jew must recognize that even natural sustenance derives from the utterance of Hashem, and this applies to divine service and Torah study, connecting each Jew to Moshe.

translations.translation: A)
And with this will be understood the eternality that is in the matter of the manna
(for the Torah is eternal),
namely, that in every place and in every time and in every situation and circumstance in which a Jew finds himself,
he must know that this [fact] that he has bread from the earth,
i.e., all the matters that he receives by means of making a vessel in a natural way,
in “all your work which you do,”
behold, “not by bread alone does man live, but by all that comes from the mouth of Hashem does man live.”
For in the matter that he receives in a natural way, there is present the “utterance of the mouth of Hashem,” which is the root and source of all matters as it is in Elokus,
until the source of all sources and the root of all roots,
which comes into the action of “all your work which you do” in this lowest world, in the time of exile and in doubled and redoubled darkness.
And likewise it is also in his divine service,
for even though his divine service is in the manner of “after Hashem you shall go,”
in a manner of iskafya and in a manner of itkafya,
nevertheless, he has the empowerment from the matter of the manna,
and to the extent that this comes in revelation.
And as understood from what is explained
regarding the matter that “in relation to Moshe it is a small thing,”
that therefore it is a small thing also for each and every one of Yisrael,
behold, likewise it is in our matter of “Behold I will rain down for you bread from the heavens,” which is in the merit of Moshe,
and Moshe instituted the blessing of “Hazaan” (the One Who sustains),
therefore this exists for each and every one of Yisrael in every place and in every time and in every situation and circumstance that he may be in.
And just as it is in divine service in general,
so too it is also in the study of Torah,
that in whatever level of Torah study it may be,
even when [it is] the child who begins to speak, whom they teach Torah,
behold, they say “Torah was commanded to us by Moshe,”
that in this study and speech he already has the matter of Moshe,
and as explained above, that the matter of the manna pertains to the recognition and knowledge that this is the matter of the Torah,
and it draws down this matter below until it becomes blood and flesh like his flesh in spirituality,
and until it becomes blood and flesh like his flesh also in physicality, literally.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the revelation of the manna's essence comes through spreading the wellsprings of the inner Torah, which prepares for and brings the true and complete redemption, when the inner dimensions will be revealed.

translations.translation: B)
And behold, the revelation of this matter is through the spreading of the wellsprings of the inner Torah outward,
which comes in revelation, at least in knowledge,
at least in the manner of an omer,
in measurement and limitation,
therefore the term “rain down” is written
(and not “dew” as in all [other] places).
And this causes that just as it was with the matter of the manna the first time,
that there was an omer per skull
(as explained above),
and afterwards they ate it and it became blood and flesh like his flesh, even in the heel of the feet,
behold, so too now the matter of the aforementioned “skull” is revealed.
And as explained above, that in every place and in every time and in every situation and circumstance that he may be in,
behold, beginning from the matter in divine service,
behold, even though in revelation he has the matter of “and until,”
nevertheless, he knows that “just as there is only One in your heart, so too there is only One in our heart,”
for in his innermost heart there is the matter of actual Oneness,
unlike in the externality, where he has the matter of the letter-substitutions of “Echad,”
and likewise it is also in Torah,
that from when the child begins to speak, etc., they teach him “Torah was commanded to us by Moshe,”
and all the more so when he has already grown in Torah study and he has the matter of the inner Torah,
behold, this reveals afterwards the inner dimension of the world.
And this becomes the proximate preparation and brings afterwards the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach,
for then the matters of the inner dimension of Atik will be in revelation,
and to the extent that then “your Teacher will no longer be concealed,”
and there will be the revelation face-to-face, as explained in Tanya, chapter 36.
And there already was a foretaste of this at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
for then there was the first time the matter of “in order to test him,”
an elevation in a manner that there would be a walk in Torah, “he will walk in My Torah,”
and just as there was a foretaste of this at the time of the Giving of the Torah, so will this be in actual revelation and very soon in the days of Moshiach
[even though the main receipt of reward is in the seventh millennium,
as explained in Tanya there in the gloss],
in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach.
